verdict.line: You lose if you trade into his empowered post-ability auto before level 6 or contest his Q3 knockup at melee range; you win if you survive to your first two item spikes and turn it into a war of attrition.

brief.thesis: This is a 46.8% win rate over 631 games with lane and solo-kill advantage both going to Aatrox, and the reason is structural: his passive (Deathbringer Stance) and Q (The Darkin Blade) reward every trade he initiates, while Jax's counter-tool, E (Counter Strike), only nullifies one attack at a time and can't be held indefinitely. Jax doesn't out-damage Aatrox in an even fight before items — he out-scales him after them. The lane is defensive by design: absorb, don't answer.

theirWindow.when: right after he casts any ability
theirWindow.what: His passive Deathbringer Stance is now armed — his next auto deals bonus true-adjacent damage and heals him off your missing HP. If you're mid-trade when this procs, back out or eat it with E (Counter Strike) up; don't just tank it on cooldown.

yourWindow.when: both his E dash charges spent
yourWindow.what: Aatrox has 2 charges on Umbral Dash for reset/disengage. With both down he can't escape or extend, so this is when you commit Q (Leap Strike) into an extended trade — he has no way to reposition around your Counter Strike stun.

start.why: 45.1% win rate over 523 games and the majority pick (69%) — the extra AD and sustain matter more here than shield block, since most of his early damage lands as a single burst-into-heal rather than sustained poke.

boots.why: 45.3% win rate over 483 games and 68.4% pick — his damage is almost entirely auto-attack and on-hit (Q, empowered post-ability auto), so flat physical reduction directly undercuts both his trade damage and his passive heal-back.

core.why: The single highest-sample core path (41.7% over 60 games with Sundered Sky/Zhonya's). Sheen proc off Empower or Leap Strike is your first real damage spike and the point where the lane stops being one-sided.
Crit-proc heal and armor scale directly against his auto-heavy, physical-leaning kit, letting you actually win extended trades instead of just surviving them.
Answers his all-in windows and his R (World Ender) burst phase — stasis through his empowered auto or through his R engage buys the fight back.

situational.when: his all-ins chain Q3 knockup into an empowered auto and you need the damage bled back over time instead of eaten instantly
you're ahead in gold and want to shred a champion who otherwise heals off missing-health procs
the game goes long and you need the extra mobility/burst to punish him once his cooldowns are down

runes.keystoneWhy: 45.6% win rate on this page versus 42.9% on the Lethal Tempo page — the bonus max HP and free sustain on your first auto every ~4s directly answers a lane where you're absorbing damage more than dealing it, and it keeps you alive through poke you can't otherwise trade back into.

summoners.why: 48.7% win rate over the Flash+Teleport combo versus 46.4% for Flash+Ignite — given the lane is defensive and you're behind on solo-kill potential, Teleport lets you reset off bad trades, hold wave state under pressure, and still show up for plates or a tempo swing instead of forcing kill pressure you don't have early.

playing.title: Keep trades to one exchange
playing.detail: Land Q (Leap Strike) into an auto and disengage rather than staying in extended range — every extra auto he lands off Deathbringer Stance both damages and heals him.

playing.title: Save E for his empowered auto
playing.detail: Don't pop Counter Strike proactively. Wait for the auto right after he uses an ability — dodging that single hit removes most of a trade's damage and denies the heal entirely.

playing.title: Never stand in his Q3 arc
playing.detail: The third cast of The Darkin Blade knocks up in melee range — step to the side rather than backing straight up, since backing up in a line keeps you inside it.

playing.title: Count his dash charges before committing
playing.detail: Umbral Dash has 2 charges. If both are down he can't reset or escape — that's your window to force a full trade with E covering his response.

playing.title: Use R to tank the engage, not extend a kill
playing.detail: Grandmaster's Might's bonus armor/MR is best popped right before he commits, softening the opening burst so you survive to your own damage window.

playing.title: Play for the Trinity Force spike, not lane kills
playing.detail: You are not favored to win all-ins before your first big item. Farm safely under tower pressure and let the matchup flip once Sheen procs are online.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win rates above are pulled from measured games on the current patch (16.18.1) via OP.GG — the mechanical reasoning and trade-timing advice are my own read of the kits, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful of Aatrox’s The Darkin Blade (Q)! Use Counter Strike [E] to block his Deathbringer Stance (P). Purchase items that reduce healing.
